matrix_and_anticoagulant:
MATRIX: human whole blood (venous, healthy donors), ex vivo; plasma harvested for the complement ELISAs.

ANTICOAGULANT FOR THE WHOLE-BLOOD / COMPLEMENT ASSAY: **NOT REPORTED.** Verbatim from Methods, "Immunotoxicity assays": "Venous blood from healthy donors was collected in anticoagulant-sprayed vacutainer tubes (Roche medical Center, Basel, Switzerland) and kept at room temperature." The anticoagulant is named ONLY as "anticoagulant-sprayed"; its chemical identity is never given, NO concentration is given, and no catalogue number is given for these tubes. The required dataset field is therefore "not reported" — do not impute one.

CRITICAL DO-NOT-CONFLATE WARNING: the paper DOES name an anticoagulant elsewhere, but for a DIFFERENT assay. Methods, "Preparation of washed platelets": "Blood from healthy volunteer donors was collected and anticoagulated in sodium citrate containing vacutainers (BD Vacutainer, #367714)", with platelets subsequently handled in ACD ("acid citrate dextrose; 39 mM citric acid, 75 mM sodium citrate, 135 mM dextrose, 0.01 U/ml Apyrase"). That sodium-citrate/ACD detail belongs to the washed-platelet (PAC-1 / P-selectin, Figs 1 and 5) workstream ONLY. It must NOT be carried across to the Figure 6 complement data. Propagating it would be a fabrication.

Incubation volumes: 195 uL fresh whole blood added in TRIPLICATE to U-bottom 96-well plates containing 5 uL of 40-fold concentrated ON stock (200 uL final). Blood used within 3 h of collection, held at room temperature until use. ONs solubilised in PBS pH 7.4 at 10 mM stock.

analytes_and_units:
ANALYTES: complement split fragments C3a and C5a (two analytes only; no C4a, no sC5b-9/TCC, no Bb, no C3b — those were not measured).

UNITS AS REPORTED AND AS PLOTTED: **Stimulation Index (SI) — a dimensionless ratio.** Verified first-hand from the Figure 6 image: panel C y-axis is labelled "C3a [Stimulation Index]" (scale 0-25) and panel D "C5a [Stimulation Index]" (scale 0-15). The local supplement grain file carries unit='stimulation_index' for all 144 values, which matches.

NO ABSOLUTE CONCENTRATIONS ARE REPORTED. The ELISA kits yield mass concentrations (typically ng/mL for C3a/C5a), but the paper never prints a ng/mL value, a standard-curve range, or an LOQ for either complement analyte. Therefore the native concentration unit for this dataset is **UNVERIFIED** — it must not be recorded as ng/mL. Only the ratio is recoverable.

Dosing: all Figure 6 oligonucleotide conditions were tested at a single concentration, **50 uM** (figure legend and results text both state 50 uM). The authors themselves flag this as "a concentration that is generally far in excess of clinically used doses". Only the cytokine arm (Fig 6E, IL-8/MCP-1) has a concentration-response; there is NO concentration-response for C3a or C5a.

Threshold line: a dashed line sits at SI ~= 2 in panels C and D (read by me from the figure image; the numeric value 2 is NOT stated in the text, so the exact value is UNVERIFIED). The legend describes it verbatim as "Dotted lines represent the 95% ULN confidence interval of unstimulated platelets" — wording that is copy-pasted from the platelet figures and is arguably incorrect for a whole-blood complement endpoint. Flagging as a legend defect, not reinterpreting it.
normalisation_definition:
DEFINITION, verbatim from Methods ("Immunotoxicity assays", final paragraph): "Triplicate values were averaged for each concentrations and stimulation index (SI, relative to PBS or scrambled ON) was calculated for each donor. Mean stimulation index for the 3 donors was used to rank the immunotoxicity potential of the test items."

So: SI = (mean of the 3 technical replicates of the treated well) / (the corresponding control for that SAME donor). The per-donor SI is the unit of analysis; the across-donor mean is used only for ranking.

WHICH DENOMINATOR APPLIES TO FIGURE 6 — resolved empirically, not guessed. The methods sentence leaves it ambiguous ("relative to PBS or scrambled ON"). The supplement settles it: in the "Figure 6" sheet the PBS condition is exactly 1.0 for every donor and both analytes (C3a PBS: 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 — min = max = 1.00; C5a PBS: 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 — min = max = 1.00). A control that is identically 1.000 with zero variance IS the denominator. Therefore for Figure 6C/D:
  SI = [C3a or C5a in the treated sample] / [C3a or C5a in the same donor's PBS vehicle control].
Conclusion: normalised to PBS vehicle, per donor. The "scrambled ON" alternative was NOT used here — no scrambled ON appears among the 16 Figure 6 conditions. (This is my inference from the data structure plus the methods sentence; it is strongly supported but the paper does not state it in so many words for Figure 6 specifically.)

INTERPRETIVE CONSEQUENCES for anyone using the 144 raw values:
 - Values are ratios; they cannot be converted back to ng/mL because no absolute control concentration is published.
 - Because PBS is the denominator, PBS carries no biological variance and must be excluded from any variance/CV estimate; including it will deflate dispersion artificially.
 - SI < 1 is meaningful here and does occur: the "Inhib." control runs 0.1-0.3 (C3a) and 0.3-0.5 (C5a), and "- PS" (ODN2395, phosphodiester) runs 0.5-1.4 (C3a) and 0.7-0.9 (C5a), i.e. at or below vehicle.
 - Donor-count inconsistency to carry as a caveat: Methods says "the 3 donors"; the Fig 6 legend says "Data represent means +/-SD (n = 5)"; the actual supplement has n=5 for most conditions but n=3 for PBS and for all three LNA conditions. All three statements cannot be simultaneously true. Record per-condition n from the supplement, not from the legend.

THE HEADLINE STRUCTURE-ACTIVITY RESULT: complement activation here tracks the CpG/TLR9 MOTIF, not the PS backbone or the length. ODN2395_Thio (CpG, full PS) gives C3a SI 11.8 and C5a SI 4.6 — comparable to the classical- and alternative-pathway positive controls. The identical-sequence phosphodiester ODN2395 gives 0.72 / 0.80, i.e. no activation. Meanwhile every non-CpG (AC)n oligo is fully phosphorothioated across 10-22 nt yet sits at SI ~1 for both analytes. This dissociates PS content from complement activation in this system and is the single most useful datum in the paper for the complement endpoint.

NUANCE I AM OBLIGED TO FLAG (my observation from the raw data, NOT an authors' claim): the blanket statement "No effect on complement split factors was seen with any of the length tool ONs" is a group-mean statement. Individual donors exceed the SI~2 dashed line for C3a at the 14-mer (max 2.0), 16-mer (max 2.6), 18-mer (max 2.7), 20-mer (max 2.1) and 22-mer (max 2.1). Donor-level C3a maxima therefore touch or cross the threshold even though the means (0.94-1.48) do not. For a risk-assessment dataset this is a real, reportable between-donor spread, not a clean null.

ENDPOINT CLASSIFICATION: this is TOXICITY / off-target innate-immune safety assessment. None of the test articles targets complement, so the "drug whose TARGET is complement = efficacy" exclusion does NOT apply here. No flag needed.

1. CpG 2006 (= PF-3512676 / CpG 7909), 24-mer: 5′-TCG TCG TTT TGT CGT TTT GTC GTT-3′ — COMPLETE PHOSPHOROTHIOATE. Ungapped: TCGTCGTTTTGTCGTTTTGTCGTT.

3. CpG 2006 P-O: "consisting of a complete phosphorodiester backbone". NOTE the paper spells it "phosphorodiester" here (the word "phosphodiester" is used correctly 3 other times in the paper — so this is a typo in the Reagents paragraph). CRITICAL GAP: the SEQUENCE of the P-O variant IS NOT SEPARATELY PRINTED. The naming ("CpG 2006 P-O") and the Results wording ("the same oligo with a complete phosphodiester (P-O) backbone") imply it is base-identical to CpG 2006, but the sequence string is never given for it. That it is base-identical is STRONGLY IMPLIED BUT NOT LITERALLY PRINTED — record as UNVERIFIED at the character level.
4. CpG 2216 (type A / CpG-A), 20-mer, as printed: GGg gga cga tcg tcG GGG GG
   Ungapped with case preserved: GGgggacgatcgtcGGGGGG
   Base sequence ignoring case: GGGGGACGATCGTCGGGGGG

PER-POSITION BACKBONE LEGEND — CONFIRMED AND FLAGGED AS ANOMALOUS:
The legend printed in this paper is, verbatim: "a mixed (P-O and P-S) backbone, with lowercase letters representing phosphodiester bonds". Applying it literally to the printed string GGgggacgatcgtcGGGGGG gives:
  - positions 1-2 (GG, uppercase) = PHOSPHOROTHIOATE
  - positions 3-14 (gggacgatcgtc, lowercase) = PHOSPHODIESTER
  - positions 15-20 (GGGGGG, uppercase) = PHOSPHOROTHIOATE
i.e. PS poly-G ends flanking a PO central CpG palindrome.

MY INFERENCE, CLEARLY LABELLED AS SUCH (not the paper's statement): this is the OPPOSITE CASE CONVENTION to the standard ODN 2216 notation. Canonical ODN 2216 is written 5′-ggGGGACGATCGTCgggggg-3′ where LOWERCASE = phosphorothioate and CAPITALS = phosphodiester (verified by WebSearch against an Enzo product sheet, patent literature and a PMC table — second-hand corroboration, consistent across sources). Mangsbo has inverted BOTH the case assignment AND the legend. The two inversions cancel: the resulting CHEMISTRY described by Mangsbo (PS poly-G ends, PO central palindrome) is IDENTICAL to canonical ODN 2216, and the base sequence GGGGGACGATCGTCGGGGGG matches canonical ODN 2216 exactly. So the compound is almost certainly ordinary ODN 2216 and the notation is merely non-standard. I am NOT asserting the paper is in error — I am recording that the printed legend is self-consistent, is the reverse of community convention, and yields the canonical molecule. Anyone re-synthesising from this paper must read the legend as printed and not assume the usual convention.

OTHER REAGENTS, verbatim: compstatin "cyclic compstatin Ac-I(CV(1MeW)QDWGAHRC)T" at 9.2 µM; C5a receptor antagonist "C5aRA AcF-(OPdChaWR)" at 8.4 µM. All oligonucleotides from Cybergene (Swedish supplier). No purity, no endotoxin level, no LAL result and no mass-spec confirmation is reported for any oligo — all UNVERIFIED and a notable methodological omission given that endotoxin would itself activate complement in whole blood.

(3) sC5b-9 — fluid-phase/soluble terminal complement complex; captured with mAb clone aE11, which reacts with a C9 NEOEPITOPE exposed on complement activation and absent from native C9 (ref 30, Mollnes 1985). Y-axis ranges: 0-150 CAU/ml (whole blood), 0-100 (plasma), 0-30 (C2-def), 0-50 (MASP-2-def), 0-6 (inhibitor panel). Figure 7 y-axis ranges (pg/ml): IL-6 0-800, IL-8 0-60000, IL-1beta 0-200, IL-2 0-300, TNF 0-10000, MCP-1 0-12000. Figure 8 y-axis ranges (pg/ml): IL-6 0-400, IL-8 0-15000, IL-1beta 0-100, IL-2 0-50, TNF 0-3000, MCP-1 0-1500. Capture antibodies: clone bH6 (anti-C3 neoepitope, in-house, ref 29); anti-factor P clone #2 (Quidel, San Diego, CA) for C3bBbP; clone aE11 (anti-C9 neoepitope, in-house, ref 30) for sC5b-9. QC: "Inter- and intra-assay coefficient of variability below 20% were accepted. When original ODs were inaccurate (>20% differences or above maximum range) and could be responsible for a change in trend, remeasurements were conducted." CYTOKINES: "Cytokines were measured in EDTA plasma samples with a 27-plex kit (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Hercules, CA) according to the manufacturer's instructions." key_results_verbatim:
ABSTRACT (verbatim): "Lepirudin-anticoagulated human whole blood and plasma was incubated with increasing concentrations of three classes of synthetic CpGs: CpG-A, -B and -C oligodeoxynucleotides and their GpC sequence controls. ... In whole blood and plasma, CpG-B and CpG-C (p<0.05 for both), but not CpG-A (p>0.8 for all) led to time- and dose-dependent increase of soluble C5b-9 (sC5b-9), the alternative complement convertase C3bBbP, and the C3 cleavage product C3bc. GpC-A, -B and -C changed sC5b-9, C3bBbP and C3bc to the same extent as CpG-A, -B and -C, indicating a DNA-backbone-dependent effect. Dose-dependent CpG-B binding was found to C1q (r=0.83; p=0.006) and factor H (r=0.93; p<0.001). The stimulatory complement effect was partly preserved in C2-deficient plasma and completely preserved in MASP-2-deficient serum. CpG-B increased levels of IL-1beta, IL-2, IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1 and TNF in whole blood, which were completely abolished by inhibition of C5 and C5aR1 (p<0.05 for all)."
KEY POINTS (verbatim): "CpG ODNs activate the complement system dependent on their backbone structure." / "CpG ODNs bind to C1q and factor H, indicating initial CP and direct AP activation." / "CpG ODNs induced C5-C5aR1 dependent proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines."
WHICH CLASSES ACTIVATED, WHICH DID NOT: "CpG-B and CpG-C ODN led to a significant dose-dependent increase in C3bc, C3bBbP and sC5b-9 levels in whole blood (p < 0.01 for all, Fig. 2) and plasma (Fig. S1), whereas CpG-A ODN had no effect on complement activation (p > 0.05) in neither whole blood nor plasma." ACTIVATED: CpG-B (ODN 2006) and CpG-C (ODN 2395). DID NOT ACTIVATE: CpG-A (ODN 2216).
BACKBONE, NOT SEQUENCE — the central claim: "Similar to CpG-A, equimolar concentrations of sequence-modified GpC-A did not result in complement activation (Fig. 3). GpC-B ODN resulted in a similar extent of complement activation as measured by C3bc, C3bBbP and sC5b-9 and were not different from CpG-B ODN. A similar trend in C3bc, C3bBbP and sCb-9 levels was observed for sequence-modified GpC-C ODN (Fig. S2). In further experiments, only CpG-B ODNs were used as the backbone is identical to CpG-C ODNs." And in Discussion: "Unlike CpG-A, both CpG-B and CpG-C share a complete phosphorothioate (P-S) backbone, explaining the differential effects on complement activation. These findings are also consistent with previous studies assessing P-S ODNs in primates and showing ODN backbone-dependent complement activation (34-36)." [refs 34-36 = Galbraith 1994, Henry 2014, Henry 1997 — all three on the ALREADY-KNOWN list.] Also: "the present study highlights that the CpG ODN structure itself, i.e. the backbone, is responsible for the complement activation". On the CpG-A null result: "The lack of immunostimulatory potential in our model may be related to the phosphodiester (P-O)/P-S chimeric backbone of CpG-A ODNs. Compared to P-O ODNs, P-S ODNs are more likely to bind to DNA-binding proteins, i.e. complement products (38). Additionally, P-S ODN-protein complexes dissociate at a much lower rate (38). We argue that these functional differences between the backbone structures may explain that the apparent threshold needed for CpG-A ODN induced complement activation was not reached in our model." On B vs C magnitude: "A different magnitude of complement activation was observed for CpG-B and CpG-C, and this might be explained by the palindrome sequence comprised in CpG-C ODN. In the presence of a palindrome sequence, secondary hairpin structures with a stem and loop could form which may contribute to additional nuclease stabilization (37). This may have positively affected complement protein binding affinity."
C1q AND FACTOR H BINDING, r AND p VERBATIM (Figure 6 panel labels, read directly off the rendered figure): factor H "r = 0.93 / p < 0.001"; C1q "r = 0.83 / p = 0.006". Text: "C1q and factor H showed a significant positive correlation between the concentration of CpG-B and either C1q or factor H (p = 0.006, p < 0.001, respectively) (Fig. 6). No binding of C2, properdin, MBL or MASP-2 to CpG-B ODN could be detected (Fig. S3)." x-axis of Fig 6 = CpG-B ODN/bead ratio at 0.2:1, 1:1 and 5:1; y-axis MFI 0-1500.
PATHWAY DISSECTION: "CpG-B ODN led to increased levels of C3bc and sC5b-9 over time (Fig. 4A). Reconstitution of C2 led to a 2- to 3-fold increase in complement activation, indicative for contribution of CP and/or LP." "A time-dependent increase of C3bc and sC5b-9 levels was observed, yet reconsitution with MASP-2 did not increase complement activation (Fig. 4B). These data suggest that the lectin pathway is not required for CpG ODN induced complement activation." "Upon CpG-B ODN stimulation, C2 inhibition led to markedly reduced levels of C3bc (p = 0.021) and sC5b-9 (p = 0.027) (Fig. 5). MBL inhibition showed no statistical effect on complement activation. Factor D inhibition led to an overall inhibition of C3bc, C3bBbP and sC5b-9 formation (p = 0.010, p = 0.046, p = 0.039, respectively)."
FACTOR H MECHANISM HYPOTHESIS: "We speculate that when factor H binds to CpG ODN, its interaction with C3b could be impaired, leaving the C3(H2O)Bb to split more C3 leading to spontaneous self-amplification and extensive sC5b-9 formation. ... In support of this, studies investigating toxicity of P-S ODNs in primates observed complement activation together with decreased plasma levels of factor H. Moreover, the addition of purified factor H prevented ODN induced complement activation (35)."
CYTOKINE-INHIBITION EXPERIMENTS: "CpG-B ODN significantly increased pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1beta, IL-2, IL-6, TNF) and chemokines (IL-8 and MCP-1) (Fig. 7). Only C5 inhibition reduced CpG ODN induced cytokine release (p < 0.05, for all). Importantly, the selective C5aR1 inhibitor PMX-53 led to cytokine reductions comparable to C5 inhibition, indicating that the effect was mediated primarily through the C5a-C5aR1 signaling axis (Fig. 8)." CRITICAL NEGATIVE RESULT: "We found complement-dependent cytokine release upon CpG ODN incubation, which was independent of TLR9 and CD14." Neither the TLR9 inhibitor ODN 4191 (30 ug/ml) nor anti-CD14 (15 ug/ml) reduced the cytokine response; only eculizumab (100 ug/ml) and PMX-53 (10 ug/ml) did. Fig 8 significance marks read off the figure: IL-6 *, IL-8 ** **, IL-1beta (no mark shown), IL-2 *, TNF (no mark shown), MCP-1 ** and ***.
CONCLUSION (verbatim): "we found that CpG ODN class-B and -C activated the complement system in a dose- and time-dependent manner. The effect appears to be CpG ODN class-dependent and triggered by physical properties of the ODN backbone. Complement activation was classical and alternative pathway mediated through interactions with C1q and factor H, respectively. CpG ODN induced cytokines release appeared to be secondary to complement activation, mediated through C5aR1 and independent of TLR9 stimulation."
EFFICACY-vs-TOXICITY FLAG (task rule): the test articles here are CpG ODNs, whose target is TLR9, NOT complement. Complement activation is therefore an OFF-TARGET / TOXICITY endpoint, correctly counted. The complement-directed agents in this paper (eculizumab, PMX-53, anti-C2, anti-factor D, anti-MBL) are TOOL INHIBITORS used to dissect mechanism, not test articles — their complement effects are not an efficacy readout for this endpoint and must not be counted as such.
TWO TYPOGRAPHICAL ERRORS IN THE ACCEPTED MANUSCRIPT, flagged so they are not propagated: (i) the Figure 1 legend reads "CpG class B and CpG class B ODNs contain a complete PO backbone" — it should read class B and class C, and P-S not PO; the figure graphic itself (rendered and inspected) correctly shows ODN-2006 and ODN-2395 as entirely phosphorothioate, and the Discussion states "both CpG-B and CpG-C share a complete phosphorothioate (P-S) backbone". (ii) Figure 3 and Supplementary Fig 2 legends give the GpC/CpG concentration as "10 uM/ml", a unit error; Methods give the correct "equimolar concentration (10 uM)".

normalisation_definition: NO stimulation index, NO fold-change and NO percent-of-control is used as a primary endpoint anywhere in this paper. Complement data are reported as ABSOLUTE concentrations in CAU/ml (complement arbitrary units per millilitre), read off in-house ELISA standard curves fitted with a sigmoidal four-parameter logistic equation in GraphPad Prism 9 after background OD subtraction. CAU/ml is anchored to an external reference, not to each experiment's own control: the method cites ref 31 (Bergseth G et al. 2013, Mol Immunol 56:232-239, "An international serum standard for application in assays to detect human complement activation products"), i.e. activated normal human serum assigned a fixed CAU value. Cytokines are likewise reported as ABSOLUTE pg/ml from the Bio-Rad 27-plex standard curves. Comparisons are made against concurrently run controls rather than by ratio: the negative control is PBS-treated lepirudin whole blood or plasma, and the internal positive control is Zymosan A at 100 ug/ml. The ONLY derived quantities in the paper are: (1) the Pearson correlation coefficients r in Figure 6, computed between the CpG-B ODN/bead RATIO (0.2:1, 1:1, 5:1 ODN molecules per bead) and the median fluorescence intensity emitted on complement-protein binding — r is a correlation, not a normalisation, and MFI is itself background-corrected by PBS-substitution negative controls run at each step (PBS in place of biotinylated ODN-2006, of plasma, of capture antibody, or of detecting antibody); and (2) the one verbal ratio in the Results, "Reconstitution of C2 led to a 2- to 3-fold increase in complement activation", which is a fold-change of reconstituted C2-deficient plasma over the same single donor's non-reconstituted C2-deficient plasma, quoted in prose only, derived from n=1, with no statistics attached. The only explicit cytokine-selection normalisation is the filter stated in Methods: "Only the cytokines in which the concentrations were significantly statistically increased (p < 0.05) compared to untreated samples were selected for further analyses" — a selection rule applied to the 27-plex, not a transformation of values. Statistics: generalised linear mixed models for time courses, with time, group and time-by-group interaction as fixed effects and DONOR AS RANDOM INTERCEPT (this is how between-donor variation is handled, in place of per-donor normalisation); paired t-tests for inhibitor comparisons against the non-inhibited CpG ODN group; Pearson for the binding correlations; no post hoc testing ("As this is an exploratory in vitro study with small sample sizes, no post hoc testing was performed"); alpha 0.05.
